title: Order detail shows no totals or payment card at all — every money field on the order is unread by admin
detail: The detail grid renders exactly four cards: Items (line 187), Shipment·AWB (215), Timeline (241) and Customer (263). Nothing on the screen renders subtotalPaise, discountPaise, spinRewardPaise, walletUsedPaise, deliveryPaise, codSurchargePaise, taxPaise, totalPaise, amountPaidPaise, appliedCoupon, paymentMethod, paymentStatus, razorpayPaymentId, cancellationReason or placedAt. A grep of the whole admin app (`totalPaise`) finds it only in the orders LIST (OrdersListPage.tsx:152), the customer profile and the reports/dashboard aggregates — never on the order it belongs to. The module even exports a ready-made `paymentPill(order)` helper (api/orders.ts:62) that is imported only by OrdersListPage. Meanwhile the web customer sees a full breakdown (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:177).
failure_scenario: A customer phones about order #BRK-48219: 'I was charged ₹1,299 but the coupon should have taken ₹300 off and ₹200 came from my wallet.' The admin opens /orders/<id> and sees only per-line amounts — no subtotal, no discount, no coupon code, no wallet used, no amount actually paid, and no indication of whether the payment was captured, is COD, or was refunded. There is no way to reconcile the order against what the server computed, which is the whole point of the screen.
fix: Add a Totals card (subtotal, discount + coupon code, wallet used, delivery, COD surcharge, GST, total, amount paid) and a Payment card (method, status pill via the existing paymentPill(), razorpayPaymentId, cancellation reason when cancelled), all read straight off the order document so the displayed numbers are the server-computed ones.

verdict.reason: Claim verified. OrderDetailPage.tsx (328 lines, the only order-detail component) renders exactly four cards — Items, Shipment·AWB, Timeline, Customer — and no money summary. Grep over all of admin/src returns ZERO hits for subtotalPaise, walletUsedPaise, spinRewardPaise, amountPaidPaise, discountPaise, deliveryPaise, taxPaise, appliedCoupon, razorpayPaymentId and cancellationReason; totalPaise appears only in the orders list, dashboard, customer profile and reports aggregates; paymentPill (api/orders.ts:62) is imported only by OrdersListPage.tsx:17. The fields are live data — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:353-363,585 writes walletUsedPaise and web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:163 shows the customer a full breakdown — so admin is the only surface blind to them. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and trivially fixable from the already-loaded order doc. Two mitigations shave severity but do not refute: (1) the Invoice button generates an HTML invoice (functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:50-56) containing Subtotal/Discount/Delivery/COD/GST/Total plus 'Payment: method · status' — but in a separate tab, and still missing wallet used, amount paid, spin reward and the coupon code; (2) PaymentsListPage shows amountPaise/method/status and links Payments→order, but not the reverse and with no breakdown. The design prototype also lacks a totals card, so this is an inherited gap rather than a deliberate omission. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the invoice path covers part of the reconciliation story; the wallet/coupon/amount-paid fields remain unreadable anywhere in admin, so the core defect stands.

title: Cancel is a one-click, unconfirmed, reasonless action that refunds money and restocks inventory
detail: 'Cancelled' is just another entry in the Update-status dropdown (rendered at line 163-171) and `onSetStatus` calls `changeOrderStatus({ orderId, status })` with no confirmation step and no `note`. That call routes to performCancellation (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts) which restocks every product, credits the customer wallet with amountPaidPaise, writes a wallet ledger row, cancels affiliate commissions and releases the coupon — all irreversible (cancelled has no outgoing transitions, enums.ts:56). The `note` parameter exists in the admin API type (api/orders.ts:110) and in the CF schema (status.ts:28) but no caller ever supplies it, so cancellationReason is always the literal fallback 'Cancelled by admin' (status.ts:74). That string is displayed to the customer (app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:295). The codebase already has a ConfirmDialog component used by sub-admin suspend and affiliate allocation.
failure_scenario: An admin means to click 'Packed' but hits 'Cancelled' one row below: the order is instantly cancelled, ₹1,299 is credited to the customer's wallet, stock is restored and the affiliate's commission is reversed, with no confirm prompt and no undo. The customer's app shows the cancellation reason as 'Cancelled by admin' with no explanation, and the admin can never record why it was cancelled.
fix: Route 'Cancelled' through a ConfirmDialog that requires a typed/selected reason and pass it as `note` to changeOrderStatus so it lands in cancellationReason and the timeline note.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact verifies. OrderDetailPage.tsx:166 wires the dropdown item straight to onSetStatus, which at line 88 calls changeOrderStatus({orderId, status}) with no confirmation and no note — I read the whole file; there is no modal or window.confirm anywhere in it. 'Cancelled' sits directly adjacent to 'Packed'/'Shipped' in the menu because ORDER_STATUS_TRANSITIONS lists them as siblings (packing: ['packed','cancelled'], packed: ['shipped','cancelled']), so the misclick scenario is concrete. The `note` parameter is provably dead: grep for changeOrderStatus across admin/ yields only the import, the one call site, and the definition, so status.ts:74's `reason: note ?? 'Cancelled by admin'` always takes the fallback, which cancel.ts:230 persists to cancellationReason and app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:295 shows to the customer. The consequences are irreversible and monetary: cancel.ts restocks, credits the wallet plus a walletTransactions ledger row, flips pending commissions to 'cancelled' and decrements affiliate.pendingBalancePaise, releases the coupon, and marks payments/{orderId} refunded — and cancelled has no outgoing transitions in either the CF TRANSITIONS map or enums.ts. Refutation attempts all fail: the server-side check only validates that the transition is legal (a misclick satisfies it), permissions don't discriminate since requireModule(req,'orders','edit') is the same permission used to mark an order Packed, and the path is the only status UI so it is plainly reachable. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. The fix is trivial and already idiomatic here — ConfirmDialog exists at admin/src/components/ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx and is used in nine less-consequential places (sub-admin suspend, affiliate allocation, spinner/content delete), and the note plumbing is already present end-to-end and just needs a reason input.

title: The Orders list streams the entire orders collection with a live listener and no limit
detail: `useOrdersList` attaches `onSnapshot(query(collection(db,'orders'), orderBy('placedAt','desc')))` with no `limit()` and no date window, while the page renders only 10 rows at a time (PAGE = 10, OrdersListPage.tsx:22). Every order document now embeds its full `items` array (checkout.ts:617-626), so each doc is several KB. The same hook is also imported by the Payments screen (PaymentsListPage.tsx:15,23) purely to build a shortId lookup map, doubling the exposure. The tab counts and the pending count are computed client-side over the whole array (countByTab, api/orders.ts:94).
failure_scenario: After a year at ~200 orders/day the admin opens /orders (or /payments) and the browser downloads ~70k order documents including every line item on first paint, then holds them all in memory with a live listener for the whole session — multi-second blank table, heavy read billing, and a re-render of the full list on every single order that changes anywhere in the store.
fix: Bound the listener (e.g. limit(200) plus cursor pagination, or a date-window query), and derive tab counts from a server-maintained counter or a per-tab count query instead of the full collection.

verdict.reason: Verified and confirmed. admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:18-22 attaches onSnapshot over collection('orders') with orderBy('placedAt','desc') and no limit/where/cursor, while OrdersListPage renders PAGE=10 rows. useLiveCollection (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts:99-124) materializes every doc into a module-level cache that survives unmount, and admin/src/lib/firebase.ts uses plain getFirestore with no persistent local cache, so each fresh session re-downloads and re-bills the whole collection. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:617-627 confirms the full items array is embedded on each order doc, none of which the list view uses. No archival/TTL job exists for orders in functions/src, and firestore.rules:68-70 permits admins to read the whole collection, so nothing truncates it server-side. The already-fixed 'Reports/Dashboard queries were scoped' item is a different path: dashboard.ts:77,211,448 do carry limit(), orders.ts does not. Also not on the known-intentional list and not unreachable. One detail of the claim is wrong but immaterial: PaymentsListPage does not double the exposure, because both screens share the same ORDERS_KEY cache entry and therefore one listener; it still pulls every order doc just to build a shortId map, since the Payment type (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:130-137) carries no shortId. The fix is non-trivial (tab counts, pending count, search and CSV export all scan the full array, so it needs a bounded window plus aggregate counts), but it is a real, fixable scalability defect.

title: Rider phone is silently discarded when the rider name is blank
detail: `const rider = name ? { name, phone: clean(riderPhone), currentDistanceKm } : null;` — if riderName is empty the entire Rider object is set to null, dropping the phone the admin just typed. The callable still returns {ok:true} and the admin UI toasts 'Shipment details saved' (OrderDetailPage.tsx:115). Because `shipDirty` compares riderPhone against `order.rider?.phone ?? ''` (line 103), the Save button stays enabled forever after the failed save.
failure_scenario: Admin has only the delivery driver's number, types 9812345678 into 'Rider phone', leaves 'Rider' blank, clicks Save shipment. Toast says saved; the phone is never persisted (rider stays null), the field still shows the typed number and the Save button never goes back to disabled, so the admin clicks it repeatedly with no effect. Clearing an existing rider's name to correct a typo likewise wipes the stored phone.
fix: Build the rider object when a name OR a phone is present (`riderName || riderPhone`), or reject the payload with invalid-argument when a phone is supplied without a name so the admin sees a real error.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real defect. functions/src/orders/shipment.ts:40-48 builds the Rider object only when the cleaned riderName is truthy, so a phone-only submit (or clearing an existing name) writes rider: null and silently discards the phone, while the callable returns {ok:true} and the audit meta records only the name. Refutation attempts all failed: (a) the shared type packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:26 declares name as string|null, so {name:null, phone} is a legal shape — the guard is not protecting a type invariant; (b) both customer surfaces already tolerate a null name (web track page line 120 renders under order.rider?.name &&; app order_tracking_screen.dart:239-240 guards rider != null && isNotEmpty), so no consumer requires the name gate; (c) rider.phone is not a dead field — OrderDetailPage.tsx:61 reads it back to seed the admin's "Rider phone" input, and grep across functions/, admin/, web/, app/, packages/shared and scripts/seed.ts shows adminAssignRider is its only writer, so nothing else re-persists it; (d) the stuck-Save consequence is real because the seeding effect (OrderDetailPage.tsx:44,55-62) uses a shipSeeded ref to seed inputs once per order id and deliberately ignores later live snapshots, so riderPhone keeps the typed value while order.rider?.phone ?? '' is '', leaving shipDirty (line 103) true and the Save button (line 229) permanently enabled after a toast that claims success; (e) the path is reachable and wired (exported functions/src/index.ts:23, called from admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:137) with no required-field validation in the UI; (f) it is not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. Severity is moderate (phone is admin-internal, not shown to customers) but it is genuine silent data loss with a broken dirty-state, fixable with `const rider = name || phone ? {...} : null`.

title: Firestore errors on the orders list and detail are swallowed and rendered as 'No orders yet' / 'Order not found'
detail: Both screens destructure only `{ data, loading }` from the live hooks (OrdersListPage.tsx:26; OrderDetailPage.tsx:26,30,31) and never read `error`, even though useLiveCollection/useLiveDoc surface it. On a snapshot error the cache sets `{data: [], loading: false, error}` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117-121, 147-150), so the list falls into its empty branch (line 124 'No orders yet.') and the detail into `!order` → 'Order not found.' (line 74).
failure_scenario: A rules deployment, an expired token, or a sub-admin whose read is denied opens /orders and is told 'No orders yet.' — an admin will reasonably conclude the store has no orders rather than that the read failed. Same on a detail page: a permission-denied read reports 'Order not found', tempting the admin to re-place the order.
fix: Surface the error state on both screens (an error row/panel with a retry) instead of collapsing it into the empty state.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. OrdersListPage.tsx:26 and OrderDetailPage.tsx:26,30,31 destructure only {data, loading} from useLiveCollection/useLiveDoc, both of which do expose `error` (firestoreCache.ts:96,130). On a snapshot error the cache emits {data: [], loading:false, error} (firestoreCache.ts:117-121) and {data:null, loading:false, error} (147-150), so the list falls to its empty branch ('No orders yet.', line 124) and the detail to !order → 'Order not found.' (line 74). Nothing compensates: no error boundary, no toast in the cache, and useOrdersList/useOrder (features/orders/api/orders.ts:18-26) are thin pass-throughs. This is not intentional in-repo style — ReturnsListPage.tsx:105-118 implements exactly the missing banner with the comment "Read error — surfaced instead of a misleading empty state" plus a permission-denied message, and PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:13,69 also reads error, so the orders screens are the outlier. Reachable: firestore.rules:69 gates orders reads on isAdmin(), which depends on the mirrored `role` custom claim, while admin sign-in (auth/api/auth.ts:39-50) only checks the admins doc and refreshes the token — a missing/stale claim or a rules deploy yields permission-denied while RequireAuth still admits the user. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Only caveat: the "reviews-only sub-admin" variant is weak since any sub_admin satisfies isAdmin(); the token/claim and rules-deploy paths carry the finding.

title: /orders is reachable by any signed-in admin regardless of orders.view, and orders.edit actions are only hidden client-side
detail: Routes under RequireAuth check only that an admin is signed in (RequireAuth.tsx:18-22); nothing checks modulePermissions. Only the Sidebar filters links (Sidebar.tsx:12). firestore.rules:69 grants order reads to `isAdmin()` — any admin role, not `can('orders','view')` — unlike the direct-write collections which use can()/canWrite(). Conversely the Update-status menu, Save shipment and Invoice buttons are rendered unconditionally on the detail page (no permission check anywhere in OrderDetailPage.tsx), while the callables enforce orders.edit (status.ts:54, shipment.ts:22, invoice.ts:23).
failure_scenario: A sub-admin provisioned for reviews only types /orders in the address bar (or follows the 'New order' notification deep link, seed.ts:856): the page loads and streams every order with customer names, phone numbers and full delivery addresses, because the rules allow any admin to read orders. The reverse also bites: a sub-admin with orders.view but not orders.edit sees an enabled 'Update status' button, clicks Delivered, and gets a generic 'You don't have permission…' toast after the round trip.
fix: Gate the route on modulePermissions.orders.view (a RequirePermission wrapper), tighten firestore.rules orders/payments reads to can('orders','view'), and disable/hide the status, shipment and invoice controls when orders.edit is false.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. RequireAuth.tsx:18-22 only checks that an admin is signed in; router.tsx puts every page behind that single guard, and a full grep of admin/src shows modulePermissions is consulted in exactly 4 places (Sidebar.tsx:12 nav filtering, QuickActions.tsx:42, SubAdminFormPage, AccountDialogs) — no route guard, no PermissionGate/403 component exists. OrderDetailPage.tsx has zero references to useAuthStore/role/permission, so Update status, Save shipment and Invoice render unconditionally. firestore.rules:68-69 gates order reads on isAdmin() (line 12: role in {super_admin, sub_admin}), which ignores modulePermissions and even the active-status check that can() (line 23-29) performs. Since packages/shared/src/enums.ts:276 defines a real 'view' action that the sub-admin form toggles and the Sidebar honours, a seeded catalog-only sub-admin (scripts/seed.ts:113-118, orders.view=false) can navigate to /orders and stream every order with customer name, phone and full delivery address — a genuine, fixable privilege-separation gap not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Partial refutation: the second half of the scenario is cosmetic only — functions/src/orders/status.ts:54, shipment.ts:22 and invoice.ts:23 all call requireModule(req,'orders','edit'), which re-reads the admin doc rather than trusting claims, so no unauthorized write is possible; the defect is the read exposure plus the missing client-side disable, not a write hole. Confidence is medium rather than high because every read rule in the file uses isAdmin() uniformly, so read-openness could be a deliberate posture (the can() helper's own comment scopes it to direct-write collections) — but that contradicts the advertised per-module view toggle.

title: Generated invoice is never invalidated — a cancelled, refunded order still offers a tax invoice for the full amount
detail: The Invoice button is enabled at every status; the first click calls adminGenerateInvoice, which renders the GST invoice and stamps invoiceUrl/invoiceGeneratedAt on the order (invoice.ts:67). Afterwards the handler short-circuits on `order.invoiceUrl` (line 124) and only reopens the stored URL — it can never be regenerated. performCancellation (cancel.ts:227-234) updates status/paymentStatus/cancellationReason but leaves invoiceUrl untouched, and the storage object stays live behind its download token. Both customer clients treat a non-null invoiceUrl as 'invoice ready': web renders a Download PDF button (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108) whose fallback copy is 'Your PDF invoice generates once the order is delivered', and the app shares it (app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:24).
failure_scenario: Admin clicks Invoice on an order that is still 'accepted' (to check the formatting), then cancels the order and the customer is refunded ₹1,299 to their wallet. The customer's Invoice page still shows 'Download PDF' and serves a tax invoice for ₹1,299 on a cancelled, fully refunded order — and the admin has no way to regenerate or revoke it.
fix: Clear invoiceUrl/invoiceGeneratedAt (and delete the storage object) inside performCancellation, restrict generation to delivered orders (matching the customer-facing copy), and let the button regenerate/refresh an existing invoice instead of only reopening it.

verdict.reason: Every assertion checks out and I found no guard anywhere. admin/src/features/orders/routes/OrderDetailPage.tsx:123-138 short-circuits on order.invoiceUrl and only reopens the stored URL; the Invoice button (line 176) has no disabled state at any status (the `cancelled` flag at line 98 only gates the shipment fields at 217-229). functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:18-68 gates solely on requireModule(req,'orders','edit') with NO order-status precondition, writes invoices/{shortId}.html with a firebaseStorageDownloadTokens token, stamps invoiceUrl/invoiceGeneratedAt (line 67), and freezes the payment state into the HTML footer (`Payment: ${o.paymentMethod} · ${o.paymentStatus}`), so a post-refund invoice still reads "paid". A repo-wide grep for invoiceUrl finds exactly one writer (invoice.ts:67) plus the initial nulls in checkout.ts:666 and seed.ts:632 — nothing ever clears it. performCancellation (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts), the single funnel for both customer and admin cancels, updates status/paymentStatus/restock/wallet-refund/commission-reversal/payments row but never touches invoiceUrl or the Storage object; the approved-return path doesn't either. firebase/storage.rules:26 denies direct client reads but its own comment states the tokened URL bypasses rules, and no token rotation or delete exists, so the object stays live. Both clients key on the field alone: web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108-119 renders "Download PDF" whenever invoiceUrl is non-null, and app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:24-28 shares it; neither hides the Invoice entry point for cancelled orders (web .../orders/[id]/page.tsx:231, OrderCard.tsx:91, app order_detail_screen.dart:104). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, reachable in one click, and fixable in a few lines (clear invoiceUrl in the cancellation transaction and/or allow regeneration — the Storage path is deterministic so it would simply overwrite). One qualifier that does not refute the claim: the web invoice page also renders its own on-screen invoice card for any status independent of invoiceUrl, so a complete fix needs status-awareness there too.
